market_behavior_description: APMC mandis shut down completely for 3 to 5 days. Farmer supply deliveries halt, causing temporary acute shortages and retail price spikes. Demand for sweets and cooking crops spikes.
Substantial rise in local vegetable demand for communal feasts and household celebrations. Mandi prices typically climb by 15-25% over a 10-day period.
Primary annual harvest arrivals flood the APMC trading floors. Prices tend to touch seasonal lows due to the high volume of fresh, non-storable crop arrivals.
Massive influx of rabi onions (highly storable) and dry wheat grains. Prices stabilize at lower levels, marking the optimal period for buyers to procure and stock dry/cold storage.
Extreme heat and water shortages in key growing districts (e.g. Pune, Ahmednagar) severely stunt vegetable growth. Supply falls short of demand, causing significant price surges.
Heavy monsoon rains lead to waterlogging on rural roads and highway transit delays. Mandi arrivals drop sharply, prompting temporary price spikes at urban wholesale points.
